Chapter Eight: The Wisdom of Simplicity—Returning to What Matters.
You know, these days, life can feel like a nonstop whirlwind. There’s always something tugging at your attention—another message, an urgent task, a new worry. It’s so easy to get swept up in this rush that we forget what’s truly important.
But imagine this: a family, usually buried under busy schedules and endless notifications, decides to escape to the countryside for the weekend. No screens, no deadlines—just each other and the quiet beauty around them. They take long walks in the woods, share simple meals, and end the day with cozy conversations by the fire. And in that peaceful space, they start to realize something surprising: a lot of what they thought was “necessary”... really isn’t.
See, most of us don’t even notice how much clutter—both in our homes and in our minds—piles up over time. The urge to collect more, do more, and stay ahead can leave us feeling restless and unsatisfied. Taoism offers a gentle nudge in a different direction. It suggests that by choosing simplicity, we actually open up space for what matters most.
Picture a retiree, sorting through a lifetime of keepsakes. At first, there’s a wave of nostalgia, even a little sadness. But as she lets go of things she no longer needs, something shifts. Each item released brings a little more freedom—a sense of lightness. And in that new, uncluttered space, she discovers room for fresh experiences, deeper connections, and unexpected joy.
Now, don’t get me wrong—simplicity isn’t about denying yourself or living with nothing. It’s really about clarity. It means figuring out what’s truly essential and allowing yourself to let go of the rest. Funny thing is, the more we chase after “more”—more stuff, more achievements, more approval—the more we end up feeling like something’s missing. Less peace, less meaning, less genuine satisfaction.
Taoism reminds us that when we simplify, we actually rediscover abundance. Not the kind that’s measured by possessions, but the richness that comes from just being—fully present, fully alive.
And here’s the heart of it: in those quiet moments, when the world slows down and your mind finally settles, what really stands out? It’s the simplest things—love, presence, gratitude, and connection. That’s the wisdom of simplicity. Life’s deepest joys aren’t hidden in what we add, but shine through in what we choose to let remain.
